skill_gaps.label: Ball handling under pressure
skill_gaps.diagnosis: The handle breaks down the moment a defender applies real ball pressure or the game speeds up, which shows up as live turnovers even when the same move looks clean in an empty gym.

drills.name: Two ball pound series
drills.cue: Keep the chest up and the eyes off the ball the entire set.

drills.name: Chair change of pace
drills.cue: Sell the hesitation with the shoulders before the burst.

drills.name: Live pressure dribble
drills.cue: Stay low enough that a slap at the ball hits your forearm, not the ball.

drills.name: Weak hand only finishing
drills.cue: Full speed approach, no slowing down to protect the weak hand.

skill_gaps.progression: Add a second defender to the pressure dribble once the player can finish the set clean twice in a row, then move the same reps into a live scrimmage possession.

skill_gaps.label: Shooting consistency
skill_gaps.diagnosis: Mechanics look fine on a slow catch and shoot but fall apart off movement or late in a session, which reads as a conditioning and repetition gap more than a form problem.

drills.name: Form shooting inside 8ft
drills.cue: One motion release, hold the follow through until the ball hits the rim.

drills.name: One dribble pull up
drills.cue: Same gather footwork on every spot, do not speed up on the catch.

drills.name: Off the catch to a target
drills.cue: Feet set before the pass arrives, not after.

drills.name: Fatigue set
drills.cue: Legs drive the shot even when tired, do not shoot arms only.

skill_gaps.progression: Once makes-after-fatigue stays within ten percent of fresh makes, add a closeout before every rep to simulate game contests.

skill_gaps.label: Finishing through contact
skill_gaps.diagnosis: Shots that go in clean at practice speed get altered or blocked once a body is attached, usually from finishing off the wrong foot or trying to avoid contact instead of absorbing it.

drills.name: Pad contact layups
drills.cue: Initiate the contact, do not wait for it to arrive.

drills.name: Off foot finishes
drills.cue: Practice the finish that feels wrong until it does not.

drills.name: Euro and hop counters
drills.cue: Sell the first step before the counter move.

drills.name: Second jump finishes
drills.cue: Land ready to go back up immediately, no dead landing.

skill_gaps.progression: Move from a padded defender to a live, physical defender once the player finishes eight of ten pad reps without altering the shot.

skill_gaps.label: Defensive footwork
skill_gaps.diagnosis: The player reaches instead of sliding, which draws fouls and lets ball handlers blow by on the first live dribble.

drills.name: Lateral slide ladder
drills.cue: Stay in a low stance, feet never fully come together.

drills.name: Closeout to slide
drills.cue: Short, controlled last two steps into the closeout, hands active but not reaching.

drills.name: Mirror drill live
drills.cue: Match the offensive player's hip, not the ball.

drills.name: Rebound and outlet
drills.cue: Find a body to box out before ball watching.

skill_gaps.progression: Add a live ball handler with a live dribble once the mirror drill stays clean for a full 45 second set.

skill_gaps.label: Conditioning and pace
skill_gaps.diagnosis: Skill quality clearly drops in the second half or fourth quarter, which limits everything else this player already does well.

drills.name: 17s court sprints
drills.cue: Full sprint both directions, walk the recovery, do not jog it.

drills.name: Suicide plus 10 makes
drills.cue: Shooting form should not change between round one and round five.

drills.name: Transition finish sprints
drills.cue: Full speed finish, not a jog-in layup.

drills.name: Free throws at fatigue
drills.cue: Same pre-shot routine every single attempt, especially when tired.

skill_gaps.progression: Track make percentage at fatigue across sessions and raise the sprint volume once it matches the fresh percentage.

positions.label: Point Guard
positions.emphasis: Pace control, ball security under pressure, and reading ball screens.
positions.recruiting_note: College staffs want to see a guard who can play fast without turning it over and who talks on defense. Live pressure reps matter more than empty gym form here.

positions.label: Shooting Guard
positions.emphasis: Off ball movement, catch and shoot speed, and creating separation off one or two dribbles.
positions.recruiting_note: Film that shows quick decisions off the catch, not just standstill shooting, is what separates recruits at this position.

positions.label: Wing
positions.emphasis: Two way versatility, transition finishing, and defending multiple positions.
positions.recruiting_note: Programs at every level are short on wings who can guard three positions and still shoot it. That versatility should be the headline of the recruiting film.

positions.label: Power Forward
positions.emphasis: Finishing through contact, defensive rebounding, and face up shooting range.
positions.recruiting_note: Modern college offenses want forwards who can step outside the paint. Combine post work with perimeter shooting reps in the film sent to coaches.

positions.label: Center
positions.emphasis: Rim protection, screen setting, and finishing above the rim.
positions.recruiting_note: Recruiters weigh verified measurements and rebounding rate heavily at this position, so track and report both alongside the highlight film.
